cus.content: ARCH rules for feat-6 (global per-repo spec numbering). Hexagonal architecture is untouched: this feature adds agent tooling and prompt rules only, and introduces no application dependency. Binding constraints for every CU in this batch: ARCH.PYTHON.EXPLICIT_DECLARATION (every variable annotated at first binding), ARCH.PYTHON.NO_ANY (no typing.Any, no bare dict/list/tuple/set), ARCH.PYTHON.SLOTTED_FROZEN_DATACLASS, ARCH.PYTHON.MONADIC_ERROR (expected failures returned, not raised through try-except). The tool must be repo-agnostic: the repository root is derived from __file__, no repository-specific bug or feature name is assumed, because the .LLMDD folder is a portable standard. A committed counter file is branch-scoped and cannot express a repo-global sequence, so the allocator reads every git ref; a sqlite counter is forbidden because a binary counter file cannot be hand-merged when two branches bump it.

LEGEND for feat-6. CU = Computational Unit. CU folder = per-CU subdirectory named after the CU id. COORDINATES.itr = DTR area affected by the CU. REQUIREMENTS.itr = what part of the feature the CU adds. IMPLEMENTATION_STEPS.itr = stepwise instructions for the Coder. ACCEPTANCE.itr = per-CU acceptance criteria plus tests. Counter = the plain-text file .LLMDD/spec-driven/ids.txt holding one kind=n line per sequence. Allocator = .LLMDD/tools/next-spec-id.py, the only sanctioned way to obtain a new bug or feature serial. Ref = a git ref under refs/heads or refs/remotes; the allocator scans every one so a serial is unique per repository across branches. Fixture = the throwaway repository the test builds under /tmp/opencode.

REQUIREMENTS: Create the deterministic allocator that makes spec ids unique per repository across branches and clones: the tool .LLMDD/tools/next-spec-id.py plus its fixture test .LLMDD/tools/test_next_spec_id.py. The allocator takes the highest serial seen in the working tree plus every git ref, both from spec filenames and from each ref's counter, then writes max+1 to the plain-text counter .LLMDD/spec-driven/ids.txt. This delivers feature criteria 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. Depends on: nothing (new files only; no shared edit with cu-002 or cu-003).

COORDINATES: FILE..LLMDD/tools/validate-steps.py, FILE..LLMDD/tools/check-advisor-approval.py. Both are the sibling typed Python tools under .LLMDD and are the reference shape for explicit annotation at first binding, no typing.Any, slotted frozen dataclasses, and exit-code discipline. .LLMDD/tools/next-spec-id.py and .LLMDD/tools/test_next_spec_id.py are creations absent from the baseline.

IMPLEMENTATION_STEPS:
1. Write the allocator to .LLMDD/tools/next-spec-id.py with the exact content below (complete file, no placeholders): ```python
"""Global per-repo spec-id allocator (feat-6).

Allocates bug and feature serials from a plain-text counter plus every git
ref, so ids stay unique per repository across branches and clones.

CLI:
    next-spec-id.py --kind bug|feature [--dry-run] [--prefix bugfix-feature]
    next-spec-id.py --check

Exit 0: clean, or an id printed. Exit 1: check violation. Exit 2: usage
error. See .LLMDD/tools/check-advisor-approval.py for the sibling shape.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TypeAlias

Serial: TypeAlias = int
SpecKind: TypeAlias = str
CounterMap: TypeAlias = dict[str, Serial]
KindMax: TypeAlias = dict[str, Serial]
Findings: TypeAlias = list[str]

COUNTER_REL: str = ".LLMDD/spec-driven/ids.txt"
SPEC_DIRS: dict[str, str] = {
    "bug": ".LLMDD/spec-driven/bugs",
    "feature": ".LLMDD/spec-driven/features",
}
FEATURE_PREFIXES: Sequence[str] = ("feat-", "bugfix-feature-")
BUG_PREFIX: str = "bug-"
REF_NAMESPACES: Sequence[str] = ("refs/heads/", "refs/remotes/")
SKIP_DIRS: Sequence[str] = ("templates",)
BUG_RE: re.Pattern[str] = re.compile(r"^bug-(\d+)-")
FEATURE_RE: re.Pattern[str] = re.compile(r"^(?:feat|bugfix-feature)-(\d+)-")
COUNTER_RE: re.Pattern[str] = re.compile(r"^(bug|feature)=(\d+)\s*$")


@dataclass(slots=True, frozen=True)
class Usage:
    """Usage problem that ends the run with exit 2."""

    message: str


@dataclass(slots=True, frozen=True)
class Violation:
    """Check failure that ends the run with exit 1."""

    message: str


@dataclass(slots=True, frozen=True)
class RefSpec:
    """One spec directory as seen at one git ref."""

    ref: str
    directory: str
    names: Sequence[str]


@dataclass(slots=True, frozen=True)
class Repo:
    """Repository root plus the resolved spec tree."""

    root: Path

    @property
    def counter(self) -> Path:
        return self.root / COUNTER_REL

    def specs(self, kind: SpecKind) -> Path:
        return self.root / SPEC_DIRS[kind]


def repo_root() -> Path:
    """Repository root is two parents above .LLMDD/tools/."""
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent


def spec_names(path: Path) -> Sequence[str]:
    """Spec filenames in one directory, empty when it is absent."""
    if not path.is_dir():
        return ()
    return tuple(sorted(entry.name for entry in path.iterdir() if entry.is_file()))


def tree_names(repo: Repo, kind: SpecKind) -> Sequence[str]:
    """Spec filenames from the working tree."""
    return spec_names(repo.specs(kind))


def ref_names(repo: Repo, ref: str, kind: SpecKind) -> Sequence[str]:
    """Spec filenames at one ref, empty when the path is absent there."""
    try:
        done: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str] = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(repo.root), "ls-tree", "--name-only", ref, "--", SPEC_DIRS[kind]],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )
    except OSError:
        return ()
    if done.returncode != 0:
        return ()
    entries: list[str] = []
    line: str
    for line in done.stdout.splitlines():
        entry: str = line.strip().rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        if entry.endswith(".md"):
            entries.append(entry)
    return tuple(entries)


def all_refs(repo: Repo) -> Sequence[str]:
    """Every branch ref in the clone, local and remote-tracking."""
    try:
        done: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str] = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(repo.root), "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname)", *REF_NAMESPACES],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )
    except OSError:
        return ()
    if done.returncode != 0:
        return ()
    return tuple(line.strip() for line in done.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip())


def ref_serials(repo: Repo) -> KindMax:
    """Highest serial per kind across every ref."""
    highest: KindMax = {"bug": 0, "feature": 0}
    ref: str
    for ref in all_refs(repo):
        kind: SpecKind
        for kind in ("bug", "feature"):
            names: Sequence[str] = ref_names(repo, ref, kind)
            pattern: re.Pattern[str] = BUG_RE if kind == "bug" else FEATURE_RE
            name: str
            for name in names:
                found: re.Match[str] | None = pattern.match(name)
                if found is not None:
                    highest[kind] = max(highest[kind], int(found.group(1)))
        text: str = ref_counter_text(repo, ref)
        key: str
        value: str
        for key, value in parse_counter(text):
            if key in highest:
                highest[key] = max(highest[key], int(value))
    return highest


def ref_counter_text(repo: Repo, ref: str) -> str:
    """Counter file text at one ref, empty when absent."""
    try:
        done: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str] = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(repo.root), "show", ref + ":" + COUNTER_REL],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )
    except OSError:
        return ""
    if done.returncode != 0:
        return ""
    return done.stdout


def tree_serials(names: Sequence[str], kind: SpecKind) -> KindMax:
    """Highest serial per kind from one set of spec filenames."""
    highest: KindMax = {"bug": 0, "feature": 0}
    pattern: re.Pattern[str] = BUG_RE if kind == "bug" else FEATURE_RE
    name: str
    for name in names:
        found: re.Match[str] | None = pattern.match(name)
        if found is not None:
            highest[kind] = max(highest[kind], int(found.group(1)))
    return highest


def merge_max(left: KindMax, right: KindMax) -> KindMax:
    """Element-wise maximum of two serial maps."""
    return {key: max(left[key], right[key]) for key in left}


def parse_counter(text: str) -> Sequence[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Parse `kind=n` lines; unknown or malformed lines are ignored."""
    rows: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    line: str
    for line in text.splitlines():
        found: re.Match[str] | None = COUNTER_RE.match(line.strip())
        if found is not None:
            rows.append((found.group(1), found.group(2)))
    return tuple(rows)


def read_counter(path: Path) -> CounterMap:
    """Counter map from disk; a missing file seeds to empty."""
    if not path.is_file():
        return {}
    try:
        text: str = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        return {}
    return {key: int(value) for key, value in parse_counter(text)}


def write_counter(path: Path, values: CounterMap) -> None:
    """Write the counter file with stable key order."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    lines: str = "".join(key + "=" + str(values[key]) + "\n" for key in sorted(values))
    path.write_text(lines, encoding="utf-8")


def next_serial(repo: Repo, kind: SpecKind) -> Serial:
    """Highest serial used anywhere in this repository, plus one."""
    highest: KindMax = merge_max(ref_serials(repo), tree_serials(tree_names(repo, kind), kind))
    other: SpecKind = "feature" if kind == "bug" else "bug"
    highest = merge_max(highest, tree_serials(tree_names(repo, other), other))
    return highest[kind] + 1


def render_id(n: Serial, kind: SpecKind, prefix: str | None) -> str:
    """Render the spec id for this run."""
    lead: str = prefix if prefix else ("feat-" if kind == "feature" else BUG_PREFIX)
    return lead + str(n) + "-"


def check(repo: Repo) -> Findings:
    """Collect every numbering violation in the working tree."""
    findings: Findings = []
    kinds: tuple[str, str] = ("bug", "feature")
    kind: SpecKind
    for kind in kinds:
        names: Sequence[str] = tree_names(repo, kind)
        pattern: re.Pattern[str] = BUG_RE if kind == "bug" else FEATURE_RE
        seen: dict[Serial, str] = {}
        name: str
        for name in names:
            found: re.Match[str] | None = pattern.match(name)
            if found is None:
                continue
            serial: Serial = int(found.group(1))
            if serial in seen:
                findings.append("duplicate " + kind + " serial " + str(serial) + ": " + seen[serial] + " and " + name)
            else:
                seen[serial] = name
    stored: CounterMap = read_counter(repo.counter)
    kind = "bug"
    for kind in kinds:
        if kind in stored:
            behind: Serial = next_serial(repo, kind) - 1
            if stored[kind] < behind:
                findings.append("counter " + kind + "=" + str(stored[kind]) + " is behind serial " + str(behind))
    roots: tuple[str, str] = (".LLMDD/DTRS", ".LLMDD/ITRS")
    root: str
    for root in roots:
        directory: Path = repo.root / root
        if not directory.is_dir():
            continue
        entry: Path
        for entry in sorted(directory.iterdir()):
            if not entry.is_dir():
                continue
            if entry.name in SKIP_DIRS:
                continue
            spec: Path = repo.root / ".LLMDD/spec-driven/features" / (entry.name + ".md")
            bug_spec: Path = repo.root / ".LLMDD/spec-driven/bugs" / (entry.name + ".md")
            if not spec.is_file() and not bug_spec.is_file():
                findings.append("orphan artifact " + root + "/" + entry.name + " has no matching spec file")
    return findings


def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser: argparse.ArgumentParser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Allocate the next bug or feature id for this repository."
    )
    parser.add_argument("--kind", choices=["bug", "feature"], help="Which sequence to draw from.")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Print the id without writing the counter.")
    parser.add_argument("--prefix", help="Id prefix for this run, for example bugfix-feature-.")
    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="Report numbering violations and exit non-zero.")
    args: argparse.Namespace = parser.parse_args(argv)
    return args


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args: argparse.Namespace = parse_args(argv)
    repo: Repo = Repo(root=repo_root())
    if args.check:
        findings: Findings = check(repo)
        if findings:
            for finding in findings:
                sys.stderr.write("VIOLATION: " + finding + "\n")
            return 1
        return 0
    kind: SpecKind = str(args.kind)
    if args.kind is None:
        sys.stderr.write("usage: --kind bug|feature is required unless --check is given\n")
        return 2
    prefix: str | None = args.prefix
    n: Serial = next_serial(repo, kind)
    stored: CounterMap = read_counter(repo.counter)
    if args.dry_run:
        sys.stdout.write(render_id(n, kind, prefix) + "\n")
        return 0
    values: CounterMap = dict(stored)
    values[kind] = max(n, values.get(kind, 0))
    write_counter(repo.counter, values)
    sys.stdout.write(render_id(n, kind, prefix) + "\n")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Fixture test for next-spec-id.py (feat-6).

Builds a throwaway repository under /tmp/opencode with bug-5 and feat-5,
cuts two sibling branches, and asserts the allocator hands out different
ids. No pytest; test_synopsis_budget.py is the standalone-script precedent.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

KIND_BUG: str = "bug"
KIND_FEATURE: str = "feature"
COUNTER_REL: str = ".LLMDD/spec-driven/ids.txt"
EXIT_OK: int = 0
EXIT_VIOLATION: int = 1
BASE: str = "refs/heads/main"
FIRST: str = "refs/heads/branch-a"
SECOND: str = "refs/heads/branch-b"
DUPLICATE_SPEC: str = ".LLMDD/spec-driven/bugs/bug-5-shadow.md"


def run(command: list[str], cwd: Path) -> str:
    """Run one command and return stdout, letting a failure raise."""
    done: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str] = subprocess.run(
        command, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
    )
    return done.stdout.strip()


def stage_allocator(repo: Path) -> Path:
    """Copy the allocator into the fixture repo so __file__ gives its root."""
    tools: Path = repo / ".LLMDD/tools"
    tools.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    source: Path = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "next-spec-id.py"
    target: Path = tools / "next-spec-id.py"
    shutil.copyfile(source, target)
    return target


def allocator(repo: Path) -> list[str]:
    """The allocator under test, staged inside the fixture repository."""
    return [sys.executable, str(stage_allocator(repo))]


def git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    """Run one git command inside the fixture repository."""
    return run(["git", *args], repo)


def make_fixture(base: Path) -> Path:
    """Create the fixture repository and return its path."""
    root: Path = base / "spec-id-fixture"
    if root.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(root)
    root.mkdir(parents=True)
    git(root, "init", "--quiet", "--initial-branch=main")
    git(root, "config", "user.email", "fixture@example.com")
    git(root, "config", "user.name", "Fixture")
    bugs: Path = root / ".LLMDD/spec-driven/bugs"
    features: Path = root / ".LLMDD/spec-driven/features"
    bugs.mkdir(parents=True)
    features.mkdir(parents=True)
    (bugs / "bug-5-fixture.md").write_text("# bug-5: fixture\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (features / "feat-5-fixture.md").write_text("# feat-5: fixture\n", encoding="utf-8")
    git(root, "add", "-A")
    git(root, "commit", "--quiet", "-m", "fixture base")
    git(root, "branch", "branch-a")
    git(root, "branch", "branch-b")
    return root


def allocate(repo: Path, kind: str, ref: str) -> str:
    """Allocate one id while checked out at ref."""
    git(repo, "checkout", "--quiet", ref.replace("refs/heads/", ""))
    out: str = run([*allocator(repo), "--kind", kind], repo)
    return out


def expect(condition: bool, label: str) -> None:
    """Record one assertion, keeping all failures visible."""
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError("failed: " + label)


def main() -> int:
    base: Path = Path("/tmp/opencode")
    repo: Path = make_fixture(base)
    first: str = allocate(repo, KIND_BUG, FIRST)
    expect(first.startswith("bug-"), "branch-a id carries the bug prefix, got " + first)
    git(repo, "add", "-A")
    git(repo, "commit", "--quiet", "-m", "bump for branch-a")
    second: str = allocate(repo, KIND_BUG, SECOND)
    git(repo, "checkout", "--quiet", "main")
    expect(second != first, "sibling branches share the id " + second)
    both: str = run([*allocator(repo), "--check"], repo)
    expect(both == "", "clean repository must report no finding, got " + both)
    shadow: Path = repo / DUPLICATE_SPEC
    shadow.write_text("# bug-5: shadow\n", encoding="utf-8")
    result: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str] = subprocess.run(
        [*allocator(repo), "--check"], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
    )
    expect(result.returncode == EXIT_VIOLATION, "duplicate serial must exit 1, got " + str(result.returncode))
    shadow.unlink()
    dry: str = run([*allocator(repo), "--kind", KIND_FEATURE, "--dry-run"], repo)
    expect(dry.startswith("feat-"), "dry-run prints a feature id, got " + dry)
    sys.stdout.write("PASS\n")
    return EXIT_OK


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# .LLMDD/tools

Repo-agnostic tooling carried by the .LLMDD standard. Every tool derives
the repository root from its own location, so the folder works unchanged
in any repository that carries a .LLMDD folder.

## next-spec-id.py

Allocates the next bug or feature serial for this repository. It reads
the plain-text counter at `.LLMDD/spec-driven/ids.txt` plus every git ref
under `refs/heads` and `refs/remotes`, so two branches cut from the same
state of dev never receive the same number.

```sh
python3 .LLMDD/tools/next-spec-id.py --kind bug
python3 .LLMDD/tools/next-spec-id.py --kind feature --prefix bugfix-feature-
python3 .LLMDD/tools/next-spec-id.py --kind feature --dry-run
python3 .LLMDD/tools/next-spec-id.py --check
```

`--kind` prints the id and bumps the counter. `--prefix` chooses the id
lead, so a bug or bugs fix prints `bugfix-feature-<n>-` from the feature
sequence. `--dry-run` prints without writing. `--check` never writes and
fails on a duplicate serial, on an artifact directory with no matching
spec file, or on a counter behind a serial present in the tree.

Exit codes follow the convention shared with `check-advisor-approval.py`:
0 clean or id printed, 1 check violation, 2 usage error.

## check-advisor-approval.py

Validates a Designer-issued approval token against a proposed change.
Exit 0 allows, 1 denies, 2 is a usage error.
